The ability to add a digital driver's license to iPhone may soon be expanding to a 15th U.S. state.

Apple currently lists 14 states, as well as Puerto Rico, that support this feature, but backend data has revealed another state is about to be added...

Many people have long looked forward to a day when they wouldn't need to carry physical identification documents, such as driver's licenses and passports, and could simply present their digital ID directly through an iPhone or Apple Watch.

That future may still be some way off, but Apple took its first step back in 2021, when the company announced plans to allow iPhone users to add their driver's license or state ID to the Wallet app. So far, 14 states have adopted this feature:

  • Arizona
  • Arkansas
  • California
  • Colorado
  • Georgia
  • Hawaii
  • Illinois
  • Iowa
  • Maryland
  • Montana
  • New Mexico
  • North Dakota
  • Ohio
  • West Virginia

Backend data discovered by MacRumors shows that Oklahoma is about to be added to this list.

We have previously provided a detailed guide on how to add your driver's license or state ID to the iPhone Wallet app. As mentioned at the time, a digital ID may not completely replace its physical counterpart, so we still recommend that everyone continue to carry their physical ID.

That said, at eligible TSA checkpoints and when verifying age with merchants, the digital version can still effectively protect your privacy. The ID will only confirm that you meet the age requirement, without revealing any personal information, such as your date of birth.
